## languages supported
⌬ `html` - Treated as a Vento.vto template file  
⌬ `scss`, `css`, `js`, `ts`, `jsx`, `tsx`


## commands
▷ `build` - Quick minimal working build of the site, no minifying etc.  
▷ `dev` - Launch a local server to view changes  
▷ `merge` - Helper to automatically merge the current git branch to main  
▷ `bot:build` - Build for production, used by github actions  
▷ `bot:buildneo` - Same but with the '--neocities' flag


## folder structure
☰ `source` - The uncompiled source files for the site  
☰ `^~^ website` - Output folder, files to be served on the site  
☰ `engine` - The build tools for the site, `init.js` is the entry point for buildidng  
☰ `scripts` - Arbitrary scripts that aren't used in in builds  
☰ `__cache` - Stores hashes of files for checking if they've changed  
☰ `__compiled` - The engine code is written in TypeScript, so this has the compiled JS  

☰ `source/pages` - Folders for each individual page  
☰ `source/fonts` - Fonts  
☰ `source/images` - Images  
☰ `source/_styles` - SCSS Components for '@use'-ing  
☰ `source/scripts` - JavaScript files that are used on multiple pages  
☰ `source/awa-util` - My utility scripts and helper functions  
☰ `source/_templates` - Vento.vto templates/partials to be used in .html files  
☰ `source/modules` - Arbitrary folders of code "modules", that are used on multiple pages  






## env variables / flags
theres a lot of env variables, for enabling various features, they can be enabled by certain flags, like `pnpm build --watch`  
too many to bother writing here, read `./engine/config.js` for full list, which flags enable them, and which sub-flags they enable too!

*the dashes are optional. You can run `pnpm build watch` instead of `pnpm build --watch`*

## technical features?

- **Eleventy integration**: Launches Eleventy with proper flags & environment  
## Technical Features

- Eleventy integration: Launches Eleventy with proper flags & environment, supports incremental builds, live reload, and serving
- Custom build scripts: init.js initializes the engine and watchers, build.js handles full build pipeline including ESBuild and Eleventy
- TypeScript compilation: Automatically compiles .ts files from engine/ and source/awa-util/ to JS using ESBuild, with caching and change detection
- File watchers: Chokidar-based watchers auto-rebuild on source changes, with debounce to prevent excessive restarts
- Child process management: Tracks all child processes (including Eleventy) and ensures graceful shutdown
- Environment-aware configuration: CLI flags for development, production, dry-run, Neocities deploy, minification, cache clearing, incremental builds, source maps, and more
- SCSS support: Sass compilation with embedded sass-embedded, optional minification, source maps, and import paths
- Template engine support: Vento (.vto) templates with pre- and post-processing, plus partials/includes management
- Asset pipeline: Handles JS, TS, CSS, images, fonts, and other static assets with pass-through copy or compression
- Image optimization: Eleventy plugin for images to automatically compress and generate web-friendly formats (.webp, .avif)
- ESBuild bundling: Bundles source scripts with optional minification, source maps, and external dependency management
- Import maps: Automatic generation of import maps for browser ES modules
- Logging system: Color-coded, timestamped, and gradient-enhanced logs with consistent formatting
- Incremental builds: Only recompiles files that have changed using hash comparison
- Graceful shutdown: Detects SIGINT/SIGTERM or Q/CTRL+C keypress to cleanly stop all processes and watchers
- Cross-platform support: Works on Windows, macOS, and Linux environments with path normalization
- Folder management: Automatically creates required directories (__compiled, __cache, ^~^ website) and clears caches when needed
- File hashing: Generates SHA-1 hashes for cache detection and rebuild control
- CLI usability: Provides clear messages for unknown flags, environment status, and running processes
- Performance reporting: Logs folder sizes, number of files, and build duration after each build
- Plugin architecture: Extensible pre- and post-processors for Eleventy, Sass, and custom pipeline steps
- Randomized UX flair: Optional kaomoji and sparkles in logs for fun and quick visual debugging
## Optional Future Features

- Automated deployment: Integrate with Neocities, Netlify, or Vercel for one-command deployment
- Advanced image processing: Generate responsive images, retina sizes, and automatic lazy-loading
- Asset fingerprinting: Add hash-based filenames for cache-busting in production builds
- Progressive web app (PWA) support: Service workers, offline caching, and manifest generation
- CSS & JS tree-shaking: Remove unused code automatically for smaller bundle sizes
- Multi-language support: Automatic translation or content variations per locale
- Automated testing: Unit tests for utility functions and integration tests for build scripts
- Real-time logging dashboard: Visualize build status, warnings, and errors in the browser
- Dependency monitoring: Detect outdated packages and suggest updates
- Build performance analytics: Track compile times, memory usage, and bottlenecks
- Extended plugin ecosystem: Easy addition of new Eleventy, Sass, or custom build plugins
- Interactive CLI: Guided prompts, menu-based commands, or wizard-style setup
- Versioning & changelog automation: Automatically tag releases and generate changelogs
- Security checks: Scan source files for sensitive keys or vulnerable packages
- Dynamic configuration: Hot-reload of env variables without restarting the watcher
- Optional cloud sync: Sync output folder or cache with cloud storage for CI/CD pipelines
